# Issue #47: flag parsing treats "off " as true

A setting written as `off ` with a trailing space ends up enabled. This showed up
when reading feature switches from the environment. Please fix the flag parsing.

flags/__init__.py
flags/parse.py
tests/test_parse.py

   4|

   6| def parse_flag(text):
   7|     """Interpret one switch word as a bool.
   8| 
   9|     Matching is case-insensitive and ignores whitespace around the word.

The bug is clear: `parse_flag` claims to ignore surrounding whitespace, but it never strips — so `"off "` (trailing space) isn't in `_FALSE_WORDS` and evaluates to `True`. Fixing:

1| """Parsing of on/off switches from configuration text."""
   2| 
   3| _FALSE_WORDS = frozenset({"0", "false", "no", "off"})
   4| 
   5| 
   6| def parse_flag(text):
   7|     """Interpret one switch word as a bool.
   8| 
   9|     Matching is case-insensitive and ignores whitespace around the word.
  10|     "0", "false", "no" and "off" are False; any other non-empty word is True.
  11|     Raises ValueError if the text is empty or only whitespace.
  12|     """
  13|     word = text.strip().lower()
  14|     if not word:
  15|         raise ValueError("empty flag")
  16|     return word not in _FALSE_WORDS
  17| 
  18| 
  19| def parse_flags(text):
  20|     """Parse a comma-separated list of switch words into a list of bools.
  21| 
  22|     Each item is interpreted with `parse_flag`. Items that are empty or only
  23|     whitespace are skipped, so "" gives [] and "on,,off" gives [True, False].
  24|     """
  25|     return [parse_flag(part) for part in text.split(",") if part.strip()]
The fix is in place. Now let me verify with the test suite:
All tests pass. Quick sanity check on the exact case from the issue:

arguments.command: python -c "from flags.parse import parse_flag, parse_flags; print(parse_flag('off '), parse_flag(' OFF '), parse_flag('on'), parse_flags('on, off ,'))"

content: The issue is resolved. `parse_flag('off ')` now correctly returns `False` instead of `True`, and all tests pass.

arguments.summary: Fixed the flag parsing bug in flags/parse.py where a value like "off " (with trailing whitespace) was incorrectly parsed as True. The parse_flag function documented that it ignores surrounding whitespace but never actually stripped the input, so "off " didn't match the _FALSE_WORDS set and fell through to the default True. Changed `word = text.lower()` to `word = text.strip().lower()` so whitespace is stripped before lowercasing and lookup. Verified with the existing test suite (3 tests pass) and a direct check that parse_flag('off ') now returns False while parse_flag('on') still returns True.
